58.why: Blind answer 3 (low) counted the doubling after round 3; IIT Guwahati's final key gives 4, the round sent at the threshold. Solution rewritten to that count.
58.solution:
Slow start begins with cwnd = 1 MSS = 2 KB and doubles every round, while cwnd is below ssthresh = 16 KB. The receiver window (48 KB) never limits these windows.

Round 1: cwnd = 2 KB. Round 2: cwnd = 4 KB. Round 3: cwnd = 8 KB. Round 4: cwnd = 16 KB.

In round 4 the window has reached ssthresh, and TCP uses congestion avoidance once cwnd is at least ssthresh. So the connection is in congestion avoidance from the 4th round of transmission: the answer is 4.

51.why: Options and solution print output patterns of *, $ and #, which the page reads as bold and maths; written as monospace LaTeX.
51.solution:
The part from Wait(A) to Signal(A) is a critical section, so the three \(\texttt{*}\) are printed one process at a time. The process that makes X = 2 prints \(\texttt{\$}\) inside that same critical section, right after its \(\texttt{*}\). So every outcome starts \(\texttt{**\$}\) and has exactly one \(\texttt{*}\) after the \(\texttt{\$}\).

No \(\texttt{\#}\) can appear before \(\texttt{\$}\), because B starts at 0 and only the \(\texttt{\$}\) process signals it. After that, each process passing Wait(B) prints \(\texttt{\#}\) and signals B again, so all three \(\texttt{\#}\) are eventually printed.

A (\(\texttt{**\$*\#\#\#}\)): the third process enters its critical section before anyone prints \(\texttt{\#}\). Possible.

B (\(\texttt{**\$\#*\#\#}\)): one of the first two processes passes Wait(B) and prints \(\texttt{\#}\) before the third process prints \(\texttt{*}\). Possible.

C (\(\texttt{**\$\#\#*\#}\)): both of the first two processes print \(\texttt{\#}\) before the third process enters. Possible.

D (\(\texttt{***\$\#\#\#}\)): \(\texttt{\$}\) is printed by the second process to enter, before the third \(\texttt{*}\). Impossible.
